title: Synthetic tool-holder seating and runout check
provenance_detail: Original synthetic guidance written for ShopfloorPilot vocabulary and safe offline evaluation; it is not copied from an equipment manual.

chunks.evidence_excerpt: In this synthetic demonstration, a vibration alarm during cutting warrants checking tool-holder seating, visible debris, runout indications, and whether the cutting load is asymmetric. These checks can separate a tool-interface condition from other possibilities; they do not establish a cause.
observable_symptoms: vibration changes with tool or load condition
chunks.possible_explanation: A tool-interface, runout, or asymmetric cutting-load condition is one possible explanation.
suggested_checks: Under the applicable operator safety procedure, inspect seating surfaces and visible tool-holder condition.
Compare repeat observations before and after a controlled tool or load change.
Check whether vibration follows the tool setup or remains with the machine.
limitations: This is synthetic advisory text with no calibrated runout or vibration threshold.
A check result must be recorded as a new observation and cannot confirm a root cause by itself.
